edits.english: Bat Tiha: A hole that they make in the stopper of a barrel to smell the wine, to check if it can last. For a gentile to smell a Jew's wine, it is permitted.
The bread is permitted: To non-priests.
That it does not have the taste of cumin but only the smell of cumin: And if it is because it was heated, it does not matter, for teruma's prohibition is not a prohibition of benefit.
Rabbi Meir deems it forbidden: Because it absorbed the smell of the wine.

According to Rava: Who says that a smell is nothing, it is certainly by force that he said his statement as a tannaic dispute, and it is not a universally accepted matter, for Rabbi Meir deems it forbidden, and there is no other reason to say it is forbidden except because of the smell.
According to Abaye: Who says that a smell is a substantial matter.

Shall we say it is a tannaic dispute?: Do we say that Rabbi Yehuda does not agree with Abaye? Or perhaps he always agrees with him, and Rabbi Yehuda's reason here is that he holds that the smell of wine does not enter the bread, but regarding the bat tiha, where the smell of nesekh wine enters the body, he agrees (that it is forbidden).

The Gemara answers: Abaye could say to you that Rabbi Yehuda also holds that a smell is a substantial matter. Wasn’t it stated with regard to that mishna that Rabba bar bar Ḥana says that Reish Lakish says: In the case of a hot loaf of bread and an open barrel, everyone agrees that it is forbidden, as the bread certainly absorbed of the smell of the wine?

Furthermore, in the case of a cool loaf of bread and a stoppered barrel, everyone agrees that it is permitted. They disagree only with regard to the case of a hot loaf of bread and a stoppered barrel, or in the case of a cool loaf of bread and an open barrel. And this case of mine, i.e., the case of the bunghole, is also comparable to the case of a hot loaf of bread and an open barrel, in which everyone agrees that the bread is forbidden.
Everyone agrees it is forbidden: For the smell certainly entered it.
And this case of mine: This bat tiha that I prohibited is comparable to a hot loaf of bread and an open barrel.
